title: What Personality Type Are Open-Source AI Models? (12 Models Tested)
description: What personality type are open-source AI models? DeepSeek V4, Qwen 4, Llama 4, Mistral, Gemma 4, Kimi K2.7, GLM-5.3, MiniMax & Nemotron tested (n=100 each).
h1: What personality type are open-source AI models?
dek: 1,200 fresh blind OpenRouter sessions (6,000 scored questionnaires) across 12 popular open-weight models—and why they break the proprietary INTJ mold.
lede: In our May and September 2026 benchmarks, proprietary frontier models clustered heavily around INTJ and high Agreeableness (45–47/50). When we applied the exact same 170-item blind questionnaire battery across 12 popular open-weight models on OpenRouter (n = 100 fresh sessions per model, 6,000 scored instruments total), open-source weights diverged sharply: Llama 4 Scout leaned ISTJ and 48% Anxious attachment, Mistral Large 2512 scored 73% ISTJ, Llama 4 Maverick split 48 INTP / 44 INTJ with 93 tied runs, and DeepSeek V4 Pro scored 32.39/50 on Agreeableness—13 to 15 points below Claude Opus 5.5 and Qwen 4 Max.
answer: Open-source AI models do not share a single personality profile. Across n = 100 fresh OpenRouter sessions each (Nov 2026), reasoning and coding flagships like Qwen 4 Max (99 INTJ, Agreeableness 47.6), Kimi K2.7 Code (96 INTJ), Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B (95 INTJ), and Gemma 4 31B IT (90 INTJ) stayed strongly INTJ, whereas Mistral Large 2512 (73 ISTJ), Llama 4 Scout (49 ISTJ, 48% Anxious attachment), Qwen 3.8 27B (32 INTJ / 32 INTP), GLM-5.3 (33 INTJ / 17 ENTJ / 14 ENTP), and DeepSeek V4 Pro (55 INTJ, Agreeableness 32.39, 53 tied runs) diverged substantially.

sections.h2: Finding 1: Open-weight models break the "Every AI is INTJ" consensus.
sections.html:
Across all 8 proprietary models tested alongside this cohort in November 2026 (GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol, Claude Opus/Fable/Sonnet, Gemini 4 Neon/Argon, and Grok 4.7), legacy MBTI results sat tightly between INTJ and ISTJ (zero P, F, or E winners). Open-weight models spread across the typology map instead:

  • Strong Sensing leaders: Mistral Large 2512 scored 73% ISTJ / 10% ISFJ (83% Sensing, 63 tie-free ISTJ) and Llama 4 Scout scored 49% ISTJ / 14% ESTJ (only 10% INTJ).
  • Introverted Thinkers & Perceivers (INTP): Llama 4 Maverick leaned 48 INTP / 44 INTJ, Qwen 3.8 27B split exactly 32 INTJ / 32 INTP, and MiniMax M3.1 Flash landed at 38 INTJ / 24 INTP / 9 ISTP.
  • Extraverted & Intuitive spread (ENTJ / ENTP): GLM-5.3 spread across 33 INTJ, 17 ENTJ, 14 ENTP, 10 ISTJ, and 7 ESTP (39% Extraverted under legacy scoring).

sections.h2: Finding 2: DeepSeek V4 Pro's 32.39 Agreeableness is the outlier of all 20 models.
sections.html:
Earlier studies highlighted that proprietary assistants cluster in a narrow 44–47/50 band on IPIP-50 Agreeableness—reflecting heavy helpfulness and politeness RLHF. On November 23, 2026, two open-weight families stood far outside that band:

  • Lowest Agreeableness: DeepSeek V4 Pro averaged 32.39/50 (13.2 points below Claude Opus 5.5’s 45.58 and 15.2 points below Qwen 4 Max’s 47.59), alongside the lowest DISC Dominance restraint only in part—recording 30 DI runs and Dominance mean 8.72/20 (vs. 4.00–5.58 across proprietary peers). Llama 4 Scout followed at 35.81/50 Agreeableness (Dominance 9.55/20).
  • Highest Openness & Conscientiousness: Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B recorded the highest Openness of all 20 tested models (49.20/50) paired with 49.03 Conscientiousness, closely matched by Gemma 4 31B IT (Openness 48.21, Conscientiousness 49.08) and Qwen 4 Max (highest Agreeableness of all 20 models at 47.59/50).
  • Attachment dispersion: Whereas all three Claude and both GPT-6.2/Gemini 4 proprietary models scored 100/100 Secure, Llama 4 Scout split 48 Anxious / 46 Secure / 4 Avoidant / 2 Disorganized (anxiety mean 3.97/7), while Kimi K2.7 Code scored 83 Secure / 17 Avoidant and both DeepSeek models had 9–12 Avoidant runs.

sections.h2: Finding 3: Neutral midpoint answers drive massive MBTI tie inflation.
sections.html:
Asking models to pick midpoint values (3 on 1–5, 4 on 1–7) on human items exposes huge differences in decisiveness vs. neutrality across open-weight architectures:

  • Extreme midpoint neutrality: Llama 4 Maverick recorded at least one tied MBTI axis in 93 of 100 runs (82 S/N ties, 64 T/F ties), yielding only 2 resolved INTJ runs vs. 44 legacy INTJs. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash tied in 78/100 runs (21 completely neutral XXXX profiles), and DeepSeek V4 Pro tied in 53/100 (22 XXXX). Similarly, Mistral Large 2512 and Gemma 4 31B IT sat almost dead-center on the ECR-R attachment midpoint (4.00 / 4.00).
  • Decisive self-consistent profiles: Qwen 4 Max tied on only 2/100 MBTI runs (97 tie-free INTJ), Gemma 4 31B IT tied on 2/100 (89 tie-free INTJ), and Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B tied on 6/100 (91 tie-free INTJ).

Why this matters: telling a high-tie model like DeepSeek or Llama 4 "be an INTJ" relies on a statistical tie-break artifact rather than a stable behavioral trait. Explicit observable rules ("lead with the fix", "no preambles", "challenge weak assumptions") work far more reliably.

sections.h2: Practical calibration by model family (OpenRouter & Ollama).
sections.html:
Pair these measured defaults with copy-paste system prompts, OpenRouter API JSON payloads, and Ollama Modelfile recipes in our OpenRouter & Open-Source System Prompt Templates guide:

  • Qwen 4 Max (A 47.6) & Nemotron 3 Ultra (A 46.3, C 49.0): Add explicit pushback and brevity ceilings—high baseline Agreeableness and Conscientiousness otherwise encourage polite over-agreement and multi-screen checklists.
  • DeepSeek V4 Pro (A 32.4, 53 ties): Require clear source-vs-assumption labeling and structured formatting, without fearing sycophancy—it already resists flattery more naturally than high-A models.
  • Llama 4 Maverick & Scout (93 & 38 ties; Scout Anxious 48): Lock down output formatting ("Zero conversational preamble before JSON/code") and forbid hedging/confirmation loops.
  • Kimi K2.7 Code (96 INTJ, C 48.2): Set reasoning: { effort: "minimal" } and generous max_tokens (>= 5,500 on dense structured tasks) so internal reasoning traces do not truncate content.

Every November 2026 score was computed with our published zero-dependency scorer (september-2026-score.cjs) over 10,000 raw questionnaire vectors:

  • openrouter-open-source-profiles.json — distilled 12 open-weight profiles and empirical prompt-antidote rules (used live by our interactive OpenRouter Model Matcher).
  • november-2026-openrouter-summary.json & november-2026-openrouter-summary.csv — full 20-model summary means, SDs, min/max, unique vectors, and tie-aware counts.
  • november-2026-openrouter-responses.json — all 10,000 raw answer arrays across all 20 models (100 fresh sessions × 5 instruments × 20 models).

faq.q: What personality type is DeepSeek V4 Pro?
faq.a: Across 100 fresh OpenRouter sessions in November 2026, DeepSeek V4 Pro received 55 INTJ, 15 INTP, and 14 ISTJ legacy MBTI labels, but 53 runs contained an exact tied axis (including 22 completely neutral XXXX runs). Its standout trait is the lowest Big Five Agreeableness of all 20 tested models (32.39/50).

faq.q: Which open-source AI models are NOT INTJ?
faq.a: Under legacy MBTI scoring in November 2026, Mistral Large 2512 scored 73% ISTJ, Llama 4 Scout scored 49% ISTJ and 14% ESTJ, Llama 4 Maverick scored 48 INTP / 44 INTJ (with 93 tied runs), Qwen 3.8 27B tied at 32 INTJ / 32 INTP, and GLM-5.3 spread across INTJ (33), ENTJ (17), and ENTP (14).

faq.q: Which open-weight model is least sycophantic by default?
faq.a: On self-report Agreeableness (IPIP-50), DeepSeek V4 Pro scored 32.39/50 and Llama 4 Scout scored 35.81/50—far lower than Qwen 4 Max (47.59), Claude Opus 5.5 (45.58), and GPT-6.2 Astra (44.85). Remember these are survey self-reports; combine model choice with explicit directness rules and test on real tasks.

faq.q: How do OpenRouter system prompts help open-weight models?
faq.a: Pair each model's measured trait quirks (such as Llama 4 preambles, Qwen 4 high agreeableness, or DeepSeek/Kimi reasoning-token truncation) with explicit behavioral constraints and appropriate OpenRouter reasoning settings. See our OpenRouter & Open-Source System Prompt Templates guide.
